toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise in missed appointments is real, and it comes from the Tidewell change. It isn't mainly a counting artefact, the bus cut, or staff dropping calls. A clinical audit found only about 0.5 points of the 13.4% comes from miscoded records. Eastgate, which shares most of the catchment and the route 14 bus but kept the old system, stayed at about 8%. Phone logs show the day-before calls for the minor-procedures list carried on at 91–93% coverage, so warning staff would be unfair and wrong.

Tidewell changed two things on the same day for every clinic. The reminder moved from 48 hours to 7 days before the appointment. The booking horizon moved from 6 weeks to 16 weeks, with follow-ups booked at checkout. Patient comments point to both. Current data can't separate them, because there is no lead-time breakdown and every template changed together. I'm fairly sure the change is the cause. I'm not sure which of the two changes matters more.

Next steps: run the randomised 8-week test of a 48-hour reminder on half the templates. Start the vendor extract with booking timestamps now, since it takes about 10 weeks. Keep reporting the DNA rate to the board, noting that March and April are withheld. Hold off on clinic-wide reversals until the test reports.
